progression.prerequisiteKnowledge: Entry knowledge: B5a (chromosome, homologous pair, diploid, haploid, sister chromatids, count centromeres), B5b (one copy, two divisions; prophase I pairing and crossing over; metaphase I either way round, independently; anaphase I partners separate; meiosis II chromatids separate; 2^n; fertilisation restores the number), B8 (four sources; reshuffle against new allele; gamete types for two genes; crossover combinations rarer; mutation inherited only in the egg or sperm line). Allele and genotype from B5b and B8. Punnett squares are not assumed (B9 comes next); the expected 1 : 2 : 1 in scene 10 is given from the gamete reasoning in one clause ("each parent gives either allele half the time") with a grey tag "Punnett squares: next video".
progression.startsWith: The hook: Two parent plants can produce a hundred seeds, and no two are quite the same. Can you predict which genotypes their offspring could have?
progression.stopsAfter: building a parent cell with colour-tracked homologues and alleles at matching positions; copying each chromosome into sister chromatids and counting by centromeres; modelling crossing over at matching points and recording the new combinations; randomising each pair with a coin and dividing twice into four gametes; listing the four gamete types without crossing over (2 x 2) and the extra crossover types; modelling random fertilisation by random draw; adding a deliberate mutation and tracing the new allele into an offspring; tallying offspring for one gene and comparing observed with expected; assessing the model (strengths, limitations, validity, reliability); evaluating a conclusion drawn from too few trials. No Punnett square method (B9), no dihybrid ratios, no linkage maps.
progression.nextLesson: Punnett squares and pedigrees (route entry bio-m5-b09).

teaching.task: How do you model meiosis, fertilisation and mutation to predict the genotypes offspring can have, and how far can you trust the predictions?
teaching.causalExplanation: (1) the model can predict which offspring genotypes are possible, and test those predictions against chance (1); (2) colours track where each chromosome came from (2); (3) matching sticker positions because homologues carry the same genes at the same places (3); (4) copying before meiosis gives two sister chromatids, still one chromosome (4); (5) breaking at matching points means a crossover exchanges the same genes, so nothing is lost or doubled, and it makes new combinations (5); (6) a coin per pair makes each pair's direction random and independent (6); (7) without crossing over there are 2 x 2 = 4 gamete types; crossing over adds rarer mixed types (7); (8) a random draw models random fertilisation and restores two of each chromosome (8); (9) only mutation makes a new allele, and only in a gamete-making cell is it passed on (9); (10) observed counts differ from expected by chance; pooling brings them closer (10); (11) assessment: what the model represents, what it leaves out, and how to keep it valid and make it reliable (11 to 13).
teaching.conversationalApproach: Opens on the hook (hook (one pair of parents, many offspring)), then works through aim and kit, step 1: build the parent cell, step 2: copy each chromosome, step 3: crossing over, step 4: line up and divide twice and the remaining scenes in order, with each reasoning stage shown on its own cue; ends with the unseen attempt (10 second countdown), brief feedback, the decision rule or board, and the key notes.
teaching.openingDecision: Two parent plants can produce a hundred seeds, and no two are quite the same. Can you predict which genotypes their offspring could have?
teaching.understandingCheck: a group models Rr x Rr but runs only four fertilisations; none gives rr; they conclude rr offspring cannot occur. Demand: evaluate. Answer: not supported; rr expected about one in four; four trials can easily give none by chance (about one time in three, (3/4)^4 = 0.32); repeat many times and pool. Crossed mistake: "the model is wrong" (it is the sample size, not the model).
teaching.curriculumScope: follows the chemistry practical format (chem-m5-p01.md, chem-m5-p03.md) and the Biology format and voice (bio-m5-b12.md). No pre-design pack exists for this route entry; this design works from the site extracts ../site-extracts/bio-m5-l08.md and ../site-extracts/bio-m5-l13.md, and from site lesson 13 Activity 3 ("Model Meiosis to Predict Gamete Variation", read in full 18 Oct) and its Predict walkthrough (AaBb unlinked gives four gamete types; expected, not guaranteed, proportions), plus lesson 08's key ideas (2n to n to 2n; crossing over in prophase I; independent assortment at metaphase I). Route entry: bio-m5-p02 ("Model meiosis, fertilisation and mutation in offspring", playlist order 16, practical-support branch, prerequisite bio-m5-b08, next bio-m5-b09). Route start: "A learner physically or interactively models the required processes." Route stop: "Prepare practical modelling of offspring genotype variation through crossing over, fertilisation and mutation; retain actual conduct/results separately." Route syllabus actions: B-genotype-practical, B-new-genotypes. Syllabus (2017, p49): B5-IQ4-01 "conduct practical investigations to predict variations in the genotype of offspring by modelling meiosis, including the crossing over of homologous chromosomes, fertilisation and mutations (ACSBL084)".

design.visualSystem: B5b's lesson-local AlleleBead (white with ink outline and letter), PairUp, CrossOver, TwoWays (the coin flip, coded in B5b, reused here as the coin), CombosGrid; B8's amber-only-for-new-allele rule and GameteList; B5a's ModelCell counting chips; the real-structure comparison plates b5x-chromosome-duplicated-pink-v1.png, b5x-chromosome-duplicated-teal-v1.png and b5x-cell-dividing-nospindle-v1.png (scenes 4 and 11, small, "the real thing"). The explainer kit (Plate, Callout, Mark, Countdown, HandText, DrawPath, scribbleEllipse, Enter), B6a's WrongChip, GreyTag, Cross, Cam. Bead chains are built in code from the painted single pop-bead plates (Codex items, shared with bio-m5-p01). New coded items: the method step rail, the colour key chip, the gamete record table, the tally table and a small expected-against-observed column chart (counts, labelled axes), the assessment card, the attempt card. - No human figures: chromosomes are bead chains on a bench; cells are loops of string; gamete cards are face-down index cards that shuffle themselves; the coin flips on its own. No hands.
design.transitionPlan: One bench persists across the practical: the step rail along the top shows where the student is, the bench holds only the beads and string the current step uses, and the right zone holds one card at a time. The parent cell is built, copied, crossed over, divided, recorded, fertilised and mutated in order, the results and assessment cards follow, the attempt card clears the bench and feedback shrinks it to a strip; scene crossfade with settle.

scenes.teachingReason: Step 1: build the parent cell: Step one: build a parent cell with two pairs of chromosomes.
scenes.narrationCue: matching positions / the same genes in the same places
scenes.motionPurpose: Build the parent cell". A string loop opens on the bench.
scenes.onScreenChange: step rail lights "1. Build the parent cell". A string loop opens on the bench. Bead chains assemble bead by bead (painted single-bead plates chained in code): long plum, long teal, short plum, short teal. On "matching positions" sticker dots (white, ink outline) land on each chain with letters on screen only: P and T on long plum (P near the top, T near the bottom), p and t on long teal at the same heights, R on short plum, r on short teal. On "the same genes in the same places" dashed level lines join P to p and T to t across the long pair, and R to r across the short pair; tag "homologous pair: same genes, same places" (grey tag "B5a"). Tag under the loop: "2n = 4". Hold about 1 second.

scenes.teachingReason: Step 2: copy each chromosome: Step two: the DNA is copied before meiosis starts.
scenes.motionPurpose: Copy". Each chain duplicates beside itself (same colours, same stickers) and a painted centromere piece (item 4) clips the two together, forming an X-like pair of bead chains.
scenes.onScreenChange: step rail "2. Copy". Each chain duplicates beside itself (same colours, same stickers) and a painted centromere piece (item 4) clips the two together, forming an X-like pair of bead chains. On "sister chromatids" the real plates b5x-chromosome-duplicated-pink-v1.png and -teal-v1.png fade in small at the right as "the real thing". On "four" B5a's counting chip counts centromeres: 1, 2, 3, 4 (each centromere piece rings in turn); a crossed chip "8 chromosomes" (grey tag "count centromeres"). Hold about 1 second.

scenes.teachingReason: Step 3: crossing over: Step three, in prophase one: crossing over.
scenes.narrationCue: prophase one / die / swap the end pieces / matching points / purple with short / white with tall
scenes.motionPurpose: Cross over (prophase I)". The long pair slides together side by side (B5b's PairUp).
scenes.onScreenChange: step rail "3. Cross over (prophase I)". The long pair slides together side by side (B5b's PairUp). On "die" the painted die (m5x-die-v1.png) tumbles on the bench and settles; code draws six pips on its blank top face (tag "six: cross over"; a small rule chip "1 to 5: no swap" sits beside it). On "Unclip" one inner plum chromatid and one inner teal chromatid separate at the bead between P and T (a small gap opens at the same bead count on both, tag "same point"). On "swap the end pieces" the two end segments exchange places (B5b's CrossOver motion), keeping their own colours (B5b rule: swapped pieces keep their parent's colour). On "matching points" a level line confirms the gap is at the same position on both; a small inset shows an unmatched swap with one chromatid gaining an extra bead and the other losing one, grey cross, tag "unmatched: genes lost or doubled". On "purple with short" the plum-top, teal-bottom chromatid rings (P with t); on "white with tall" the teal-top, plum-bottom chromatid rings (p with T). The gamete record table opens in the right zone with the line "new combinations: P t, p T". Hold about 1 second.

scenes.teachingReason: Step 4: line up and divide twice: Step four, in metaphase one: line the pairs up across the middle of the cell.
scenes.narrationCue: metaphase one / coin / random / sister chromatids / four gametes
scenes.motionPurpose: Line up (metaphase I), divide twice (meiosis I, II)". A coded dashed equator draws across the loop; both pairs slide onto it.
scenes.onScreenChange: step rail "4. Line up (metaphase I), divide twice (meiosis I, II)". A coded dashed equator draws across the loop; both pairs slide onto it. On "coin" B5b's TwoWays coin flips over the long pair (heads: plum left) and again over the short pair (tails: plum right), each result pinning a small tag. On "random" the second flip's tag reads "decided separately". On "apart into two new loops" the homologous partners separate to opposite sides and two new string loops close around them (tag "partners separate; centromeres stay joined", grey tag "B5b"). On "sister chromatids" each loop splits again, centromere pieces unclipping, into four small loops. On "four gametes" each small loop gets a "n = 2" tag and its alleles print beside it. Hold about 1 second.

scenes.teachingReason: Step 5: record the gametes, and run it again: Step five: record each gamete's alleles on a card, then rebuild and run it again with different coin results.
scenes.motionPurpose: Record and repeat". Each gamete's letters write onto a blank card plate (item 6) which slides into the record table.
scenes.onScreenChange: step rail "5. Record and repeat". Each gamete's letters write onto a blank card plate (item 6) which slides into the record table. The bench resets with a quick rewind; the die rolls a three (code draws three pips; tag "no swap this run") and the coins flip differently; new, unmixed gametes drop in. The table sorts into two blocks: "no crossover: P T R, P T r, p t R, p t r" with "2 x 2 = 4 = 2^n" (grey tag "site: confirm 2^n"), and "with a crossover: P t R, P t r, p T R, p T r" with a smaller font and the tag "less common: only on a six". On "like your die" the die rolls once more beside the table. Grey tag "B8". Hold about 2 seconds.

scenes.teachingReason: Step 6: fertilisation by random draw: Step six: fertilisation.
scenes.motionPurpose: Fertilise". Two card stacks sit at the left and right of the bench, labelled "parent 1 gametes" and "parent 2 gametes".
scenes.onScreenChange: step rail "6. Fertilise". Two card stacks sit at the left and right of the bench, labelled "parent 1 gametes" and "parent 2 gametes". On "shuffles" each stack shuffles itself (cards riffle in code). On "one at random" one card flips from each stack (P T r and p t R). On "together in one loop" their bead chromosomes join in one string loop; tag "zygote: 2n = 4". On "Record its genotype" the line "Pp Tt Rr" writes on a tally sheet; on "return the cards" both cards slide back into their stacks and reshuffle. Hold about 1 second.

scenes.teachingReason: Step 7: add a mutation: Step seven: mutation.
scenes.narrationCue: new allele / neither parent had / new one
scenes.motionPurpose: Mutate". One gamete card is drawn; its R sticker peels off and an amber sticker lands in the same place, labelled "R*" (tag "new allele", B8 rule: amber only for a new allele).
scenes.onScreenChange: step rail "7. Mutate". One gamete card is drawn; its R sticker peels off and an amber sticker lands in the same place, labelled "R*" (tag "new allele", B8 rule: amber only for a new allele).
